newsitem.title: CANADA: West demand fuels another jump in Canada spot gas.
newsitem.headline: West demand fuels another jump in Canada spot gas.

text.p: Strong demand in the western U.S. and frosty domestic temperatures continued on Wednesday to fuel the surprising recent surge in Canadian spot natural gas prices, trading sources said.
"All pipes out of Alberta are running full out," said a Calgary-based marketer. "There's strong demand in California and the Pacific Northwest and it's cold in Alberta."
Domestic and export prices in British Columbia also jumped another few notches, continuing a two-week uptrend.
Gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was talked at about C$1.58 per gigajoule, up almost 15 cents from last week.
November AECO gas was said to be fetching C$1.535 per GJ, up from C$1.41 on October 23.

Temperatures in Alberta fell earlier this week to below freezing, which boosted the demand for gas in the province. One trader said about 750 million cubic feet per day was being withdrawn from all three of the province's facilities.
In B.C., gas at the Huntington/Sumas border point rocketed to as high as US$2.20 per million British thermal units, 40 cents above last week and twice as high as September levels.
"It all depends on California," said a Vancouver-based trader. "As long as demand those utilties are pulling gas, B.C. and the Rockies will stay up." -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
